description: This case study is the results and conclusions report of an ambient loop thermal energy network feasibility study prepared for the City and County of Denver Office of Climate Action, Sustainability and Resiliency in June 2025, funded through the Climate Protection Fund that Denver voters passed in 2021. The foreword explains that the city's thermal sector, energy for heating buildings, is its hardest decarbonisation challenge, especially downtown and for buildings on Xcel's district steam system, whose customers need an all-electric alternative in the near term. The report weighs direct electrification, described as the most disruptive and expensive option, against district energy alternatives: all-electric low-temperature hot water, dual-fuel hybrid low-temperature hot water and green steam from electric boilers, and prefers the ambient loop because it can use existing infrastructure, reduce disruption and score highest on energy grid resilience. Access: PDF, free; no licence is stated. Caveats: only the foreword and opening sections were read, so modelling detail and cost figures are not verified here. It suits urban heat decarbonisation planning, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

outcomes: The study argues that an ambient loop is the best option for decarbonising thermal energy for downtown buildings, including customers of the Xcel district steam system, because it reuses existing infrastructure, avoids the cost and disruption of a new pipe network, scores highest on grid resilience and avoids the most disruptive and expensive path of building-by-building electrification.
